title: Man killed by police was no criminal, family says
article: The family of a homeless man killed by police officers last Friday say police should correct reports linking the man with a theft. He was not the suspect police were pursuing at the time, they say.
The daughter of 58-year-old Michael Vann Hubbard told lawyer David Eby that Mr. Hubbard is not suspected of stealing from a parked car in downtown Vancouver.
"This was not the guy who broke into the car," said Mr. Eby, executive director of the B.C. Civil Liberties Association.
"The family's very upset," he said, "It's not fair to them, it's not fair to his memory, and they need to set the record straight."

Police initially reported that two officers approached Mr. Hubbard as a suspect of a car break-in on Granville Street after a 911 call. Police said they shot the man after he advanced holding a box cutter and ignored demands to drop the weapon.
While the man's family knew him to be homeless and addicted to alcohol, Mr. Eby said Mr. Hubbard had no criminal record or history of violence and does not deserve to be associated with any crime.

While it's unknown why Mr. Hubbard was holding the box cutter, Mr. Eby said it's possible the man was expecting police to ask him to identify any sharp objects before searching his bag. "It's entirely within the realm of possibility that this gentleman was anticipating their request in attempting to hand over the knife."
